question: Why Aren't My Product Variations Showing on the Product Page?
metaDescription: The attribute usually isn't marked "used for variations," or the specific variation combination was never actually created after adding the attribute.
shortAnswer: The most common cause is an attribute added to the product but not explicitly marked "used for variations" in the Attributes tab — without this checkbox, the attribute displays as plain product information rather than becoming a selectable option. The second most common cause is adding or changing an attribute without then generating (or regenerating) the actual variations in the Variations tab, since WooCommerce doesn't automatically create variations just because an attribute exists.

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

WooCommerce treats "having an attribute" and "having variations based on that attribute" as two genuinely separate steps — an attribute can exist purely as descriptive product information without ever becoming a selectable variation option, which is intentional but easy to overlook when setting up a variable product for the first time.

Common Causes

  • The attribute not marked "Used for variations" in the product's Attributes tab, the single most common cause of variations simply not appearing at all.
  • Variations never generated after adding or changing attributes — the Variations tab has a specific "Generate variations" action that needs to be run, since this doesn't happen automatically.
  • The product type itself not set to "Variable product" in the Product data dropdown, still left on "Simple product" despite attributes being configured.
  • Individual variations set to a status that excludes them (out of stock and hidden from the frontend, for instance), making them technically exist but not display as purchasable.
  • A caching issue serving a stale version of the product page from before variations were properly configured.

How to Fix It

  1. Confirm the product type is set to "Variable product."
  2. Check the Attributes tab and confirm the relevant attribute(s) are marked "Used for variations."
  3. Go to the Variations tab and generate variations if they haven't been created yet, or regenerate after an attribute change.
  4. Check each variation's individual status and stock settings.
  5. Clear any caching after making changes.
